correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥2 and 1≤k≤n, cube and capped-cube support functions select all positive Gaussian coordinates or the k largest positive coordinates. Their width difference exactly equals sums of smallest positive and negative magnitudes divided by Gaussian norm. A binomial sign count gives the equality formula. For sign-group sample size b/n→1/2, the half-normal order statistic lemma sums m=O(sqrt(n)) smallest magnitudes as m²/(2 b sqrt(2/pi))+o_P(1), using uniform-to-exponential spacings with quantified O_P(n^1/4) maximal deviations and inverse-CDF error o_P(1). Binomial CLT then gives Q_c(Z); spherical normalization is handled by norm/sqrt(n)→1. Delta expansion of cube width gives Gaussian variance 1−3/pi and is exactly independent of Gaussian signs. Hence joint convergence and the zero atom. Executed standalone verifier checked 1400 independent finite support cases and 1080 seeded asymptotic diagnostics; they are corroborative, not all-dimensional proof. Boundary c=0 is scaled chi-square and c<0 has no zero atom.

originality.rationale: The same object has established lattice/Ehrhart geometry, in/circumradii and John ellipsoids, and the cube-width Gaussian CLT is classical. Read original and indexed full texts provide no implication of the finer-order random cap-minus-cube defect. A hypersimplex order-one width CLT does not imply the smaller loss of an independence polytope. The exact width-equality binomial criterion and central-rank chi-square/atomic transition are distinct invariants. Residual unindexed equivalent reformulations remain possible; lack of retrieval alone is not treated as proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Searches of indexed mathematical findings and selected arXiv full text are not exhaustive; an equivalent law may appear under trimmed half-normal sums, Gaussian knapsack or capped-cube projections.

The order-statistic lemma uses standard exponential spacing results; its application to simultaneous positive and negative Gaussian sign groups is explicitly proved, but an earlier statement of the final geometric implication may be unindexed.
No independent external audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Uniform-matroid independence polytopes are canonical families of prisms and generalized-permutahedron-related objects. Their equal-rank deterministic Euclidean transitions were studied, but the exact probability that a random width detects the cap and its critical square-root-rank scaling are natural, geometrically meaningful observables. The result proves a sharp change from a scaled chi-square at c=0 to an atomic non-Gaussian law when c>0, with a two-sided positive-part-square law below threshold. It isolates a fluctuation of order n^{-1/2}, invisible to the known cube-width order-one CLT, and establishes asymptotic independence of those scales. This is not a numerical table or a trivial reparametrization; it gives an exact finite event probability and an infinite-family limiting geometric phase transition.
